description: Twin-engine ("bimotor") light aircraft of the Somoza-era Fuerza Aérea de Nicaragua; hit by FSLN small-arms fire while flying a low-level reconnaissance run over Condega on the afternoon of 7 April 1979 and forced down near the town slaughterhouse; coming to rest largely intact. After the July 1979 Sandinista victory a local cultural committee dragged the airframe onto the hill beside the municipal cemetery; where it became the centrepiece of a public park and mirador at Km 185½ of the Pan-American Highway; a viewing tower was added later. Reported abandoned and deteriorating for years; then restored/tidied as a municipal tourist site; photographed oxidised but intact in March 2024. Manufacturer; model and serial are NOT established by any source found: contemporary Nicaraguan reporting says only "avión bimotor de la FAN". The FAN's twin-engine light types in 1979 included the Cessna 337/O-2A "Push and Pull" (e.g. FAN-315; damaged in a separate action on 29 May 1979); which is the most plausible candidate; but no source examined identifies the Condega airframe; so every identity field is deliberately left blank. Field verification or a clear photograph is needed.
